newsitem.title: POLAND: Seasonal factors seen behind Polish jobless rise.
newsitem.headline: Seasonal factors seen behind Polish jobless rise.

text.p: Less seasonal jobs in the agriculture and construction sectors pushed Poland's unemployment rate slightly up in November, acting labour minister Maciej Manicki said on Thursday.

"Unemployment traditionally increases at the end of one year and at the begining of the ensuing year as there are less jobs in agriculture and construction because of weather factors," Manicki told a news conference.
The November unemployment rate increased to 13.3 percent of the workforce -- which represents 2.306 million people -- from 13.2 percent in October. It stood at 14.7 percent in November 1995.
Manicki said the number of unemployed was likely to further rise to between 2.330 and 2.340 million people in December and then go up again in January before starting to fall again.
He said November's unemployment increased in 42 of Poland's 49 provinces and was below nine percent in several large urban regions, while above 20 percent in some northern provinces.
